mn117:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn117:1.3: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn117:2.1: ‘Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the Noble right concentration with its supports and with its requisites.
mn117:2.2: Listen and heed well what I shall say.’
mn117:3.1: ‘And what, bhikkhus, is the Noble right concentration with its supports and with its requisites?
mn117:3.2: These are right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness;
mn117:3.3: any unification of mind equipped with these seven factors—
mn117:3.4: this is called the Noble right concentration with its supports and with its requisites.
mn117:4.2: And how does right view come first?
mn117:4.3: He understands wrong view as wrong view, and he understands right view as right view: this is his right view.
mn117:5.2: ‘There is nothing given, nothing offered, nothing sacrificed, no fruit or ripening of good and bad kammas, no this world, no other world, no mother, no father, no spontaneously born beings, no good and virtuous monks and divines that have themselves realized by direct knowledge and declare this world and the other world.’
mn117:6.2: There is twofold right view, I say, bhikkhus:
mn117:6.3: there is right view affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence;
mn117:6.4: and there is the Noble Ones’ right view unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path.
mn117:7.1: ‘And what, bhikkhus, is right view affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence?
mn117:7.2: ‘There is what is given and what is offered and what is sacrificed, and there is fruit and ripening of good and bad kammas, and there is this world and the other world, and mother and father, and spontaneously born beings, and good and virtuous monks and divines that have themselves realized by direct knowledge and declare this world and the other world.’
mn117:7.3: This, bhikkhus, is right view affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence.
mn117:8.1: ‘And what, bhikkhus, is the Noble Ones’ right view unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path?
mn117:8.2: Any understanding, understanding faculty, understanding power, investigation-of-dhammas enlightenment factor, right view as path factor, in one whose mind is noble and taint-free, who possesses and develops the Path—
mn117:8.3: this is called, bhikkhus, the Noble Ones’ right view unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path.
mn117:9.1: ‘He makes effort to abandon wrong view and to enter upon right view: this is his right effort.
mn117:9.2: Mindful he abandons wrong view, mindful he enters upon and abides in right view: this is his right mindfulness.
mn117:9.3: So these three dhammas run and revolve around right view, that is to say: right view, right effort, and right mindfulness.
mn117:10.2: And how does right view come first?
mn117:10.3: He understands wrong intention as wrong intention, and he understands right intention as right intention: this is his right view.
mn117:11.2: Intention directed to sensual desires, intention directed to ill-will, intention directed to cruelty—
mn117:12.2: There is twofold right intention, I say, bhikkhus:
mn117:12.3: there is right intention affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence;
mn117:12.4: and there is the Noble Ones’ right intention unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path.
mn117:13.1: ‘And what, bhikkhus, is right intention affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence?
mn117:13.2: Intention directed to renunciation, intention directed to non-ill-will, intention directed to non-cruelty:
mn117:13.3: ‘this, bhikkhus, is right intention affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence.’
mn117:14.1: ‘And what, bhikkhus, is the Noble Ones’ right intention unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path?
mn117:14.2: Any thought, thinking, intention, fixing, fixedness, directing of mind, verbal process, in one whose mind is noble and taint-free, who possesses and develops the Path—
mn117:14.3: this, bhikkhus, is the Noble Ones’ right intention unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path.
mn117:15.1: ‘He makes effort to abandon wrong intention and to enter upon right intention: this is his right effort.
mn117:15.2: Mindful he abandons wrong intention, mindful he enters upon and abides in right intention: this is his right mindfulness.
mn117:15.3: So these three dhammas run and revolve around right intention, that is to say: right view, right effort, and right mindfulness.
mn117:16.2: And how does right view come first?
mn117:16.3: He understands wrong speech as wrong speech, and he understands right speech as right speech: this is his right view.
mn117:17.2: False speech, malicious speech, harsh speech, gossip—
mn117:18.2: There is twofold right speech, I say, bhikkhus:
mn117:18.3: there is right speech affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence;
mn117:18.4: and there is the Noble Ones’ right speech unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path.
mn117:19.1: ‘And what, bhikkhus, is right speech affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence?
mn117:19.2: Abstinence from false speech, abstinence from malicious speech, abstinence from harsh speech, abstinence from gossip—
mn117:19.3: this, bhikkhus, is right speech affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence.
mn117:20.1: ‘And what, bhikkhus, is the Noble Ones’ right speech unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path?
mn117:20.2: Any abstaining, abstention, reabstention, abstinence, from the four kinds of verbal misconduct, in one whose mind is noble and taint-free, who possesses and develops the Path—
mn117:20.3: this, bhikkhus, is the Noble Ones’ right speech unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path.
mn117:21.1: ‘He makes effort to abandon wrong speech and to enter upon right speech: this is his right effort.
mn117:21.2: Mindful he abandons wrong speech, mindful he enters upon and abides in right speech: this is his right mindfulness.
mn117:21.3: So these three dhammas run and revolve around right speech, that is to say: right view, right effort, and right mindfulness.
mn117:22.2: And how does right view come first?
mn117:22.3: He understands wrong action as wrong action, and he understands right action as right action: this is his right view.
mn117:23.2: Killing living beings, taking what is not given, misconduct in sensual desires—
mn117:24.2: There is twofold right action, I say, bhikkhus:
mn117:24.3: there is right action affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence;
mn117:24.4: and there is the Noble Ones’ right action unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path.
mn117:25.1: ‘And what, bhikkhus, is right action affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence?
mn117:25.2: Abstinence from killing living beings, abstinence from taking what is not given, abstinence from misconduct in sensual desires—
mn117:25.3: this, bhikkhus, is right action affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence.
mn117:26.1: ‘And what, bhikkhus, is the Noble Ones’ right action unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path?
mn117:26.2: Any abstaining, abstention, reabstention, abstinence, from the three kinds of bodily misconduct, in one whose mind is noble and taint-free, who possesses and develops the Path—
mn117:26.3: this, bhikkhus, is the Noble Ones’ right action unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path.
mn117:27.1: ‘He makes effort to abandon wrong action and to enter upon right action: this is his right effort.
mn117:27.2: Mindful he abandons wrong action, mindful he enters upon and abides in right action: this is his right mindfulness.
mn117:27.3: So these three dhammas run and revolve around right action, that is to say: right view, right effort, and right mindfulness.
mn117:28.2: And how does right view come first?
mn117:28.3: He understands wrong livelihood as wrong livelihood, and he understands right livelihood as right livelihood: this is his right view.
mn117:29.2: Scheming, talking, hinting, belittling, pursuing gain with gain—
mn117:30.2: There is twofold right livelihood, I say, bhikkhus:
mn117:30.3: there is right livelihood affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence;
mn117:30.4: and there is the Noble Ones’ right livelihood unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path.
mn117:31.1: ‘And what, bhikkhus, is right livelihood affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence?
mn117:31.2: Here, bhikkhus, a disciple of the Noble Ones abandons wrong livelihood and gains his living by right livelihood—
mn117:31.3: this, bhikkhus, is right livelihood affected by taints, which partakes of merit and ripens into the essentials of existence.
mn117:32.1: ‘And what, bhikkhus, is the Noble Ones’ right livelihood unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path?
mn117:32.2: Any abstaining, abstention, reabstention, abstinence, from wrong livelihood, in one whose mind is noble and taint-free, who possesses and develops the Path—
mn117:32.3: this, bhikkhus, is the Noble Ones’ right livelihood unaffected by taints, which is supramundane and a factor of the Path.
mn117:33.1: ‘He makes effort to abandon wrong livelihood and to enter upon right livelihood: this is his right effort.
mn117:33.2: Mindful he abandons wrong livelihood, mindful he enters upon and abides in right livelihood: this is his right mindfulness.
mn117:33.3: So these three dhammas run and revolve around right livelihood, that is to say: right view, right effort, and right mindfulness.
mn117:34.2: And how does right view come first?
mn117:34.3: In one of right view, right intention is brought to be; in one of right intention, right speech is brought to be; in one of right speech, right action is brought to be; in one of right action, right livelihood is brought to be; in one of right livelihood, right effort is brought to be; in one of right effort, right mindfulness is brought to be; in one of right mindfulness, right concentration is brought to be; in one of right concentration, right knowledge is brought to be; in one of right knowledge, right deliverance is brought to be.
mn117:34.4: So, bhikkhus, the way of one in the higher training has eight factors, while the Arahant’s has ten.
mn117:34.5: Here too, through right knowledge, many evil unprofitable dhammas that have vanished come to perfection through development.
mn117:35.2: And how does right view come first?
mn117:35.3: In one of right view, wrong view is abolished.
mn117:35.4: And the many evil unprofitable dhammas that come to be with wrong view as their condition are also abolished in him.
mn117:35.5: And the many profitable dhammas that have right view as their condition come to perfection in him through development.
mn117:35.6: In one of right intention, wrong intention is abolished …
mn117:35.7: in one of right speech, wrong speech is abolished …
mn117:35.8: in one of right action, wrong action is abolished …
mn117:35.9: in one of right livelihood, wrong livelihood is abolished …
mn117:35.10: in one of right effort, wrong effort is abolished …
mn117:35.11: in one of right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is abolished …
mn117:35.12: in one of right concentration, wrong concentration is abolished …
mn117:35.13: in one of right knowledge, wrong knowledge is abolished …
mn117:35.14: in one of right deliverance, wrong deliverance is abolished.
mn117:35.15: And the many evil unprofitable dhammas that come to be with wrong deliverance as their condition are also abolished in him.
mn117:35.16: And the many profitable dhammas that have right deliverance as their condition come to perfection in him through development.
mn117:36.1: ‘So, bhikkhus, there are twenty parts on the profitable side, and twenty parts on the unprofitable side—
mn117:36.2: this discourse on the Dhamma in forty essential parts has been set rolling and cannot be stopped by any monk or divine or god or Māra or Divinity or anyone in the world.
mn117:37.1: ‘Whatever monk or divine, bhikkhus, should think that this discourse on the Dhamma in forty essential parts ought to be censured and rejected, then there are ten legitimate grounds for criticism that would provide him, here and now, with grounds for blame:
mn117:37.2: if that worthy one censures right view, then those monks and divines who have wrong view are honoured by him, are commended by him;
mn117:37.3: if that worthy one censures right intention, then those monks and divines who have wrong intention are honoured by him, are commended by him;
mn117:37.4: if that worthy one censures right speech …
mn117:37.11: if that worthy one censures right deliverance, then those monks and divines who have wrong deliverance are honoured by him, are commended by him.
mn117:37.12: Whatever monk or divine, bhikkhus, should think that this discourse on the Dhamma in forty essential parts ought to be censured and rejected, then these ten legitimate grounds for criticism would provide him, here and now, with grounds for blame.
mn117:38.1: ‘Even those of Okkalā, the Vassa and Bhañña, holders of the doctrine of non-causality, the doctrine of non-action, and the doctrine of nihilism, did not think that this discourse on the Dhamma in forty essential parts should be censured and rejected.
mn117:38.3: For fear of blame, attack, and confutation.’
mn117:38.4: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn117:38.5: The bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
